title: Gabčíkovo-Nagymaros Project (Hungary/Slovakia)
summary: The Court applied the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, treating its rules on treaty termination and suspension (including material breach under Article 60 and the customary rules reflected in the Convention) as applicable, and held that a state of necessity is not a ground for terminating a treaty. It confirmed that a party may not terminate or suspend a treaty except on grounds recognised by the law of treaties.

title: Military and Paramilitary Activities in and against Nicaragua (Nicaragua v. United States of America)
summary: The Court addressed the prohibition of the threat or use of force and held that the principle in Article 2, paragraph 4, of the United Nations Charter also reflects customary international law. It examined the right of self-defence under Article 51 and the conditions of necessity and proportionality.
